summary: Bangkok's everyday holy-basil stir-fry is a quick, satisfying meal: garlic, chilli and meat cooked with pungent kaphrao leaves, usually served with rice and often a fried egg. For a convenient specialist version, Phed Mark by Ekkamai BTS lists pork and beef with three spice levels. A neighborhood stall may be cheaper, but exact prices and hours vary.
whyGo: Taste a familiar, widely eaten Thai meal with a distinctive peppery holy-basil aroma and adjustable chilli heat.
Rice and a fried egg make it a filling, fast lunch; adding the egg is traditional, though add-on pricing depends on the shop.
Phed Mark is an easy-to-reach specialist stop if you want a focused restaurant meal rather than choosing a stall at random.
bestFor: Travellers who enjoy savoury, garlicky food and can choose their preferred chilli level
An easy lunch between Bangkok activities
Food-curious visitors who want to try an everyday Thai favourite
skipIf: You need a reliably mild dish without confirming the chilli level at the counter
You require a meat-free or allergy-safe meal without checking sauces and cooking practices
duration: Allow 30–60 minutes at Phed Mark for the meal and a possible queue; this is a planning estimate, not a published wait time. A busy street stall may be quicker.
cost: Phed Mark's current online menu lists kaprao pork at THB 105 and beef at THB 155. Confirm whether rice, egg, or any extras are included when ordering. Budget less at a neighborhood stall, but no current stall price was verified.
hours: Phed Mark lists Monday–Saturday 11:00–17:00 and Sunday closed. Other Bangkok shops set their own hours; check the chosen place on the day.
bestTime: For Phed Mark, go near opening or outside the lunch peak, allowing time for a queue. For street food, choose a stall actively cooking and check that it is serving when you arrive.
gettingThere: Phed Mark is at 928 Sukhumvit Road, directly in front of Ekkamai Bus Terminal and about a one-minute walk from Ekkamai BTS (Exit 3). For other stalls, choose one near your itinerary and use its exact map pin.
booking: Treat this as a casual walk-in meal; reservation availability was not stated on the restaurant site. Its menu offers normal, medium and Phed Mark heat levels. Start conservatively if you are unsure about chilli tolerance.
accessibility: Step-free entry, accessible toilets, seating clearance and specific allergy procedures were not verified. Contact the selected restaurant if these are essential.
practicalTips: Ask for pad kaphrao (ผัดกะเพรา), and add khai dao (fried egg) if you want the usual rice plate accompaniment.
The defining herb is holy basil (kaphrao), not the sweeter Thai basil used in other stir-fries.
The dish commonly includes fish sauce or other sauces; ask about ingredients for dietary needs. A meat-free order is not automatically vegetarian.
Phed Mark's price and hours are useful for that specific venue, not a promise about citywide stalls.
decemberNotes: Pad kra pao is an everyday dish, not a seasonal event. No special December 2026 hours were posted; confirm holiday opening directly, especially around Christmas and New Year.
uncertainties: Phed Mark's menu does not clarify in the viewed listing whether rice and fried egg are included in the listed prices.
Queue length, current stock, accessibility and holiday hours are not guaranteed.
Ingredients and chilli strength vary between vendors; no allergen-safe or vegetarian preparation was confirmed.
